GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: VISION. The portal is the front of the unit, not a copy of its documents. A reader arrives with a task, finds the one page that answers it in under a minute, sees at once which baseline revision they are reading and who owns it, and can follow any rule to its source clause and back to every place that cites it. The portal is a projection of the charter and, later, of the Registry. It is never a second source. PRINCIPLES. (1) One source: charter/ and registry/ are authored; the portal generates. (2) Task first, role second: five task entries, with a role hint in the wording. Research by NN/g and GOV.UK found that audience-only menus fail because readers do not know which group they belong to. (3) A map as the front door, with plain pages behind it: one clickable map with one level of detail, and a text version. SAFe and Disciplined Agile show the pattern and its risk, which is a map that overwhelms. (4) Layers from why to what to how to evidence, with a short summary before the full text and no more than two levels of disclosure. (5) Every diagram is readable by everyone: a visible text version beside it, light and dark contrast, and a click-through to the clause. (6) The baseline is visible on every page: revision, date, owner, change history. (7) Russian first, English second, with an honest marker where the text exists in one language only. (8) Quiet and fast: static files, no external requests, readable on a phone, printable. ORDER AND STRUCTURE. Home (purpose in one sentence, the map, the five task entries, the baseline stamp). Start here (five paths, each three to six pages in reading order). The big picture (the map). Why and what: Statement of Intent, Charter, Business Model. How we operate: Operating Model with its five control loops, Portfolio Management Model with its four portfolio loops, Solution Lifecycle Model, AI Policy. Do it: the six workflows (a diagram first, then the steps), the five guides, the thirteen templates as forms to copy. Reference: Vocabulary, Document Catalog, change history. Later: control and evidence, the live Registry views, clearly labelled as dated records and separate from the approved baseline. PAGE SHAPE. Title, one-line purpose, owner, revision and date tags; a five-line summary; the diagram with its text version; the clauses with permanent links and a line for where each is cited; related pages, one forward and one back; change history; report a problem. A defined term links to the Vocabulary and the Vocabulary entry lists where the term is used. VISUAL SET. The map for the whole unit. A loop diagram for each of the nine loops, in the same visual grammar. A swimlane with a role table for each workflow. A decision flow for escalation. A matrix of the 32 controls with text status tags, and a filter, in the later Registry change. An annual calendar showing the monthly, quarterly, and December yearly Steering. A Now, Next, Later view for the roadmap in the later change. JOURNEYS. Executive Sponsor or Board: home, summary, the map, the Charter and Operating Model summaries, two to four pages, with a print or PDF summary. Function head or Domain Owner: Start an AI initiative, then the engagement workflow, the Initiative Brief template, and the decision log in the later change. Delivery team member: the Solution Lifecycle Model, the service delivery workflow and guide, the templates and the Acceptance Checklist, with search as the main tool. Control function or internal audit: the AI risk and control workflow, then each control with its rule clause, its owner, and its evidence record, a stable address for each control, and an export. New joiner: one Start reading path through the numbered chapters and the Vocabulary. WHY GENERATE FROM THE CHARTER MARKDOWN. The charter is about 90,000 words with 1,000-plus numbered clauses, many tables, and 70-plus diagrams. The portal foundation authors each page as JSON from a copy of the source, which works for two pages and fails for forty: it would create a second model and the two would drift. Generating from the Markdown keeps one model and lets the build prove the links, the clause references, and the language keys. The controlled form of the charter Markdown makes a small converter safe: headings, numbered clauses, tables, lists, links, emphasis, and Mermaid fences. markdown-it-py is installed on the host. WHY KEEP THE EXISTING GENERATOR. The portal foundation already carries the O!Bank tokens and fonts, the Russian-first paths and the language switch, the build-and-check discipline (key parity, links, assets, contrast, repeatable build), the browser check with evidence, and the deployment tool behind the access policy. A site framework such as Astro Starlight has better built-in search, language routing, and reader features, and it was the recommendation of the first research. It would, however, replace the tokens, the checks, the build, and the evidence that exist, for features that this change can build in a small generator: clause links, backlinks, term links, pre-rendered diagrams, and a search index. The decision is to extend the generator and to revisit a framework only if the features cost more than the migration. WHY RENDER THE DIAGRAMS AT BUILD TIME. Runtime Mermaid needs a script, injects inline styles that conflict with a strict content security policy, and is hard to theme for dark mode. Build-time SVG has no runtime dependency, can use the portal theme variables, and can carry a title and a description. A click from a diagram step to a clause is added by the build from the clause references, not by Mermaid click handlers, which need a loose security setting. WHY THE REGISTRY COMES LATER. The Registry holds names and live state. Showing it needs a decision on audience and personal data, a clear separation from the approved baseline ("as of" date, read-only), and generated views for the controls, decisions, appointments, backlogs, roadmap, and calendar. The charter pages carry no personal data and can be published first. EVIDENCE BASE. Patterns from SAFe, Disciplined Agile, the GOV.UK Service Manual and Design System, the UK AI Playbook and Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard, the NIST AI RMF Playbook, Microsoft Responsible AI, GitLab and 37signals handbooks, Atlassian Team Playbook, Open Practice Library, Diataxis, and NN/g guidance on progressive disclosure, audience navigation, tables of contents, and tooltips; accessibility patterns from W3C WAI. Public bank AI pages stop at principles and show no accountable structure, so the government and standards sources are the better models. Several bank pages could not be read, so the bank evidence is thin.

Alternatives.Alternative: Adopt Astro Starlight: native Russian and English routing, per-language search with Russian stemming, maintained. Rejected for now because it replaces the brand tokens, checks, browser evidence, and build that exist, and it needs a Node toolchain and build-time Mermaid on top.
Docusaurus: built-in versioning and a Mermaid theme. Rejected for now for the same migration cost, and its React weight.
MkDocs Material: the richest reader features, but it is in maintenance mode, supports one language per project, and keeps Mermaid in a closed shadow root.
Keep authoring each page as JSON: simple for two pages, but a second model of about 90,000 words that drifts from the charter.
Publish PDFs or a wiki page set only: no map, no clause links, no search, no baseline stamp, and no check that the links hold.

An audience-first menu (executive, function head, team, audit): rejected as the main navigation because readers do not know their group, and content gets duplicated. Roles stay as hints in the task wording and in the reading paths.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Whether the first publication may show the English charter text under a Russian interface with markers, or the Russian text of the first layers must exist first. The proposed order of translation is the home, the start-here paths, the map and the five-line summaries, then the Statement of Intent, the Charter, the Business Model, the Vocabulary, then the rest.
The search implementation: a small index and script built by the generator, or the Pagefind binary if it can be installed without network access. Russian word forms need at least a simple stemmer.
The audience and the personal data of the Registry views, and whether the names of the Holders appear.
Whether to keep every published baseline at its own address (for example /v/1.0/) so that a link to a revision keeps working, and how the "outdated version" notice appears.
Print and PDF: a print stylesheet only, or a combined print page per layer, and whether a PDF of the whole charter is a deliverable.
The accessibility target is WCAG 2.2 AA from the foundation. The text alternative of the map and of each diagram is part of this change; a screen-reader review of one diagram is proposed.
The interface language Kyrgyz stays out.
The terms in the glossary popups: touch and keyboard behaviour (tooltips fail on touch), so a term is a link with a short preview rather than a hover-only tooltip.

Scenarios.Scenario: The Executive Sponsor opens the portal before a meeting. The home page shows the map and the baseline stamp. In two clicks they reach the Operating Model summary and the yearly Steering description, and they print one page.

A head of function wants to start an AI initiative. The task entry leads to a path of four pages: the engagement workflow, the Initiative Brief template, who approves and clears it, and what happens after the MVP. They copy the template and follow a link from the approval step to the clause.

A Solution Engineer needs to know who accepts a Feature and who releases a Solution. Search for "acceptance" returns the Solution Lifecycle Model 7.3 first, and the acceptance chain diagram links each step to its clause.

An internal auditor wants the rule behind a control. They open the AI risk and control workflow, follow a step to the clause, see where else the clause is cited, check the change history of the document, and copy the stable address into a working paper.
A new joiner is sent one link. The Start reading path walks the Statement of Intent, the Charter, the Operating Model summary, their own workflow, and the Vocabulary, in Russian where it exists.
